notJoined.title: Not on the network.
notJoined.body: This build joins none: the peer-to-peer layer is not written yet, so there is nothing here that could truthfully report on one.

notify.heading: Notifications.
notify.body: Nothing announces itself yet, because nothing has happened that would be worth announcing. What does work is the sending of one, on this device, and it can be tried here.
notify.message: Notifications arrive on this device. Nothing else has anything to announce yet.

outcome.sent: Sent. Some devices do not draw one while this window is the one in front.
outcome.refused: This device does not permit notifications from Almena. That is changed in its own settings, not here.
outcome.failed: It could not be sent, and this build cannot say why.

about.heading: The network.
about.body: Which network this node belongs to, who it is, and how many peers it is talking to. A dash is not a zero: it means nobody measured that, which is the case for all three until the peer-to-peer layer exists.

peers.heading: Peers
peers.looking: Nobody has counted yet. This is the first look since the screen opened, and whatever it finds — peers, or the reason there are none — takes the place of this.
peers.noNetwork: There is no network for a peer to be on: the peer-to-peer layer is not written yet. The list itself is here and working — the first peer to exist appears in it without this screen changing.
peers.none: This node is on a network and is talking to nobody on it. That is an answer rather than a gap: somebody counted, and the count was none.
peers.lookedAt: Looked at {{time}}, and again every ten seconds.

control.heading: Running this node
control.body: What an operator can do to it from here. The terminal offers the same two.
control.zone: Zone, or empty for this network's own
control.joinTheMesh: Take a place on the mesh
control.carriedBy: Relay to be carried by, or empty to be dialled directly
control.claimBody: Whoever sustains the network earns the right to write on it, and that has to attach to somebody. The node asks; approving is theirs to do, with their own key.
control.challengeShown: Show this to whoever contributed the node. It is good for a day, and nothing but this node remembers it.
control.certificate: Certificate (PEM), or nothing to answer in the clear

reason.alreadyOnANetwork: This node is already on a network. A second one would be a second history for one identity.
reason.noRandomness: The system would not produce randomness, so there is no key to be. A node with a guessable key is worse than one that did not start.
reason.noClock: The system would not say what time it is, and a network has to record when its first epoch began.
reason.noDirectory: This computer would not say where the node keeps things, so it has nowhere to be a node.
reason.unreadableIdentity: There is a key in the node's directory and it cannot be read. It has been left alone: writing over it would be quietly becoming a different node.
reason.recordWouldNotStart: The record would not take the acts that start it, so the network was not opened. Nothing is half-open: this node is as it was.
reason.unreadableRecord: There is a record in the node's directory and it cannot be read. It has been left alone: opening a network on top of it would put this node on a second one.
reason.recordDoesNotAddUp: The record no longer holds everything this node has already signed for. It has not come up, rather than serve a history that contradicts what it has told other people.
reason.directoryHeld: Another node is already running on this directory. A node is a directory with a key in it, and two of them over one would be a single identity with two histories.
reason.directoryCannotBeHeld: This filesystem will not say whether another node is using the directory. Starting anyway would mean guessing that nobody is — network drives often cannot answer this.
reason.noCertificate: The certificate file is not there, cannot be read, or holds no certificate. The interface has not come up: serving in the clear having been asked not to would be the worst of both.
reason.noPrivateKey: The private key is not there, cannot be read, or holds no key. A certificate and its key are one decision, and one without the other is not it.
reason.certificateAndKeyAreNotAPair: That key does not belong to that certificate. Found here rather than by the first person who fails to connect.
reason.zoneSilent: The zone did not answer, so whether anybody is already there is unknown. Nothing was opened: reading silence as an empty zone is how a second network gets started beside the one that was already running.
reason.thereIsANetwork: The zone says there is already a network. A node joins one when somebody is there and opens one only when nobody is.
reason.notThePromisedNetwork: Somebody listed as being on this network turned out to be on another one, or to be passing off one they made up. Nothing was written down — the question is asked before anything is.
reason.noTransport: This machine would not give the node a way onto the mesh at all.
reason.meshAddressUnavailable: That port could not be listened on — usually somebody else already has it. It has not quietly taken another: a node whose port moved is a node whose published record is now wrong, and nobody reading it would be told.
reason.noNetwork: There is no network to serve yet.
reason.notAClaim: That is not a challenge and an approval of it. A typo or a half-copied line — nothing was written down, and nothing is wrong with the node.
reason.notTheirs: It read, and it does not bind: the approval is not signed by the key their own record authorises, or the challenge had stopped being good. A binding that cannot be checked would be this node's word about somebody who never agreed.
reason.notWrittenDown: The record would not take it, which should not be reachable. Worth looking at the node rather than at whoever was being claimed for.
reason.addressUnavailable: Nothing could listen on that address.
reason.unknown: It did not work, and this build has no reading for what came back.

ai.body: An agent runs beside this application, on this computer. What you type reaches it over a pipe and nothing else: it is a separate program, it is handed nothing about you, and the only host it talks to is the model server it was pointed at.
ai.heading: Ask the agent.

empty.notBundled: The agent is built from its own repository and staged into the bundle, and this build was made without one. Nothing here is broken — there is simply no program to ask.
empty.notStarted: The agent has not been started. It starts when you ask it something, which takes a moment the first time and nothing after that.
empty.willNotStart: It is in this build and it would not run. What it said on the way down is in the records, which is the only place it could say anything at all.
empty.stopped: It was running and it is not now. Asking something else starts a fresh one.

conversation.adopted: Answering a question asked before this page opened. What it says cannot be shown here.

error.heading: That did not work.
error.agent_will_not_start: The agent would not start, so there was nothing to ask.
error.agent_stopped: The agent stopped part-way, so the answer never finished.
error.run_already_in_flight: The agent is already answering something. It does one thing at a time.
error.model_unreachable: Nothing answered at the model's address. Almena does not run a model — one has to be serving on this computer for the agent to reach.
error.model_unknown: That address is serving, and it does not serve the model chosen in Settings.
error.resource_unknown: The agent was asked for something it does not hold.
error.unknown: The agent refused, and this build has no words for the reason it gave. It is written down in the records exactly as it arrived.

agent.heading: The agent.
agent.body: What is running beside this application, and what it was built to ask. Every figure here is measured from the agent that is actually running — where none is, there is nothing to measure and a dash says so.

appearance.heading: Appearance.
appearance.body: How Almena is drawn on this device. Dark is the design and what a device with no opinion gets; light is there for the rooms and the people it suits better. The identity colour is the one colour on a screen that means “this is Almena” or “this is the thing you came here for” — nothing else wears it, and the application icon is the icon whichever is chosen.

language.heading: Language.
language.body: Almena opens in the language this device asks for, so there is nothing to do here until that is the wrong one. Choose a language and it is remembered from then on; leave it alone and changing the device's own language changes Almena's with it.
language.label: Interface language

openAtLogin.heading: Open at login.
openAtLogin.body: The system opens Almena when you log in, with no window: it waits in the tray until you ask for it. This is only about who starts it — Almena runs in the tray whenever it is running, whether it was opened at login or by you.
openAtLogin.label: Open Almena at login
openAtLogin.refused: The system did not accept the change, so the setting stays as it was. Its own settings are where a refusal like this is undone.

model.heading: Model.
model.body: Which model the agent is asked for. Almena runs no model itself and does not go looking for one: it asks whatever is serving on this computer, at the address the agent was built with. Nothing here has asked that server what it actually holds — this is the list Almena knows how to ask for, not the list this computer can answer.
model.label: Model the agent asks for
model.inForceNone: Running now: nothing. The agent starts when you first ask it something.
model.restartHeading: This applies the next time the agent starts.

cli.recordsNone: Not being written to a file. This node has nowhere it may keep one.
